extraction_text: Bhishma narrated a parable about three fish to illustrate the importance of timely action and foresight.
In the parable, three fish (Foresighted Fish, Timely Fish, and Hesitant Fish) lived in a shallow pond.
Fishermen arrived, drained the pond, and the Foresighted Fish immediately escaped to a deeper pond.
The Hesitant Fish was caught and killed by the fishermen due to inaction.
The Timely Fish pretended to be caught, then escaped when washed in clean water.
Bhishma concluded the parable with teachings on wisdom, time, place, and proper action.
Yudhishthira acknowledged Bhishma's wisdom and requested further teachings on handling emergencies.
